title: Mary, mother of the Church (CCC 963–970)
hook: her role points always to her son

segments.voice: Yesterday, the communion of saints: the living, the dead, and the saints, one family. Your line was one family. Whose name did you say out loud? Today, the one Catholics call the mother of that family. Day three hundred twenty-three.

There's a kind of icon, very old, that you'll find in Greek, Russian and Catholic churches alike. Mary is holding the child Jesus on one arm. Her face isn't turned to you, exactly. And her other hand is open, palm up, gesturing toward the child. The icon has a Greek name, Hodegetria: she who shows the way. People sometimes imagine Catholic devotion to Mary as a spotlight on her. In this picture, she's pointing away from herself. Today, what the Church says her role is, in one gesture.
screen: `AN OLD ICON.` → `HER HAND POINTS TO THE CHILD.` → `SHE WHO SHOWS THE WAY.`

segments.voice: First, her last words in the Gospels. At a wedding in Cana, the wine runs out. Mary tells Jesus, then turns to the servants and says, in the Douay-Rheims: "Whatsoever he shall say to you, do ye." That's the last thing John's Gospel records her saying. Not look at me. Do what he tells you. Second, the cross. Near the end, Jesus sees his mother and the disciple he loved standing by. "Woman, behold thy son." Then to the disciple: "Behold thy mother." And from that hour, John says, the disciple took her into his own home. Catholics read that disciple as standing for every believer: Jesus giving his mother to the whole Church. During the Second Vatican Council, Pope Paul VI gave her the title Mother of the Church. Third, what the Catechism says about her role. Her place in the Church can't be separated from her union with Christ. It calls her the Church's model of faith and love. She prays for the Church as a mother prays for her children. And the Catechism is careful: her role in no way hides or takes away from Christ as the one mediator. It shows his power. Fourth, where Christians differ. Orthodox Christians honor her deeply as Theotokos, God-bearer, and ask her prayers too. Many Protestants honor her as the mother of Jesus and a model of faith, but don't pray to her. Catholics pray the Hail Mary, which begins with the angel's greeting in Luke: "Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women." And at the middle of the prayer, it names her son: Jesus.
screen: `WHATSOEVER HE SHALL SAY, DO YE.` · `BEHOLD THY MOTHER.` · `IT SHOWS CHRIST'S POWER, NOT HERS.` · `WHERE CHRISTIANS DIFFER.` · then, large: `SHE POINTS TO HIM.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: one Hail Mary for the Church. Settle, and breathe. If you pray it, pray one Hail Mary slowly, for the whole Church: its people, its wounds, its saints and sinners. Let each phrase take a breath. If you don't pray it, picture the old icon instead: the mother, the child, the open hand. Follow where the hand points, and rest your attention there. The bell holds the time.
Mary. The mother of Jesus, whom Catholics call Mother of the Church: a model of faith, whose whole role, the Church says, is to point to her son. Today's word.
Your line: she points to him. Today, when someone praises you, try pointing past yourself, to the people or the grace that made it possible. Day three hundred twenty-three.

howItsDone: Catholics pray the Hail Mary on its own and in the rosary, and since 2018 keep the memorial of Mary, Mother of the Church, on the Monday after Pentecost.

notes: Douay-Rheims John 2:5, 19:26–27 and Luke 1:28 given from memory; confirm wording.
'The last thing John's Gospel records her saying': Mary speaks at Cana and is silent at the cross in John; confirm framing.
Paul VI proclaimed Mary Mother of the Church on 21 November 1964; Pope Francis instituted the memorial on the Monday after Pentecost in 2018. Confirm.
The Hodegetria icon is described as found in Greek, Russian and Catholic churches; confirm.
Summary of Orthodox and Protestant views of Mary is brief and meant to be fair; Keeper should check.

Editor review (2026-10-01): cut 'the oldest pictures of her have her pointing away from herself' (false as a general claim: early catacomb images do not); 'that's why Paul VI...' no longer claims a cause; 'the first disciple' (superlative not in CCC 963–970) changed to 'model of faith', following CCC 967; 'every line of it ends up pointing to her son' replaced with the plain fact that the Hail Mary names Jesus at its middle; added the 2018 decree to sources.
